full_judgment: 2. The case of the petitioner is that, the land in question under CS plot No.268 was requisitioned by the Government under LA Case No.10/63-64 along with other lands and after such requisition the physical possession was handed over to the then DIT at present RAJUK in the year 1964 for extension of Gulshan Model Town After taking possession DIT left the land unutilized for several years and thereafter requested the Deputy Commissioner in the years: 1969 for de-requisition and release. The Ministry concern also decided to withdraw the whole LA Case and restore possession of the recorded tenants and accordingly directed the DIT to vacate and hand over the possession of the land; The DIT at present RAJUK prepared a lay out plan wherein portion of CS plot No. 268 was marked as plot No.5 Road No. 29, Gulshan Model Town and after the aforesaid de-requisition the said plot still numbered as plot No.5 Road No.29, Gulshan Model Town; The petitioner owned 10.60 decimals of land in the said plot by way of purchase sand enjoying the possession of the same; The Petitioner has khatian in support of his claim and also his name has been properly mutated during the Dhaka Mohanagar survey in Mohanagar khatian number 1649 as Plot No.7433. The petitioner also refunded the compensation taken by the his predecessor is interest vide challan No. 36 dated 22-12-2002, though the High Court Division in writ petition No. 835 of 1977 declared illegal the demand of authority regarding return of compensation; The petitioner while in possession of the land in question entered into an agreement with a developer company for construction of a six storied building after obtaining approved plan from RAJUK; Despite knowledge of these facts the respondents with ill motive most illegally and in an arbitrary manner allotted the plot in question in favour of the respondent No. 8 vide the impugned letter of allotment; The petitioner made several representations and lastly served notice demanding justice upon the respondents and thereafter finding no other alternative remedy moved this application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.
